models_evaluated: commercial CT-based AI software for acute intracranial hemorrhage detection (unnamed)

links.outcome: Reading order and early diagnosis rate of AIH cases before vs after AI prioritization
links.effect: Early diagnosis rate rose from 0.49 to 0.76 (P=0.013); median reading order of AIH cases fell from 7.25 to 1.5 (P<0.001); Kendall's Tau fell from 0.61 to 0.01.
links.quote: Additionally, the early diagnosis rate significantly increased [from 0.49 (0.34-0.63) to 0.76 (0.60-0.93), P = 0.013], and the daily median reading order of AIH cases significantly decreased [from 7.25 (Q1-Q3: 3-10.75) to 1.5 (1-3), P < 0.001] after the implementation.

links.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic performance with vs without AI assistance
links.effect: No significant differences in accuracy (0.99 to 0.99, P=0.343), sensitivity (1.00 to 1.00, P=0.859), or specificity (1.00 to 0.99, P=0.252) after AI implementation.
links.quote: There were no significant differences in accuracy [from 0.99 (95% confidence interval: 0.99-1.00) to 0.99 (0.98-1.00), P = 0.343], sensitivity [from 1.00 (0.99-1.00) to 1.00 (0.99-1.00), P = 0.859], or specificity [from 1.00 (0.99-1.00) to 0.99 (0.97-1.00), P = 0.252] following the implementation of the AI software.

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world clinical workflow impact of implementing an AI triage/reprioritization system for intracranial hemorrhage detection on radiologists' reading order and time to diagnosis.
